name: Charlie Hickey
bio: A young man of Lord Alfred Douglas's circle, described by Douglas in his Autobiography (1929) as 'a charming boy about a couple of years younger than myself and well known to Oscar, a son of Colonel Hickey' - which, Douglas having been born in 1870, would place his birth around 1872. He was with Douglas in Paris in May 1895 while Wilde's second trial was proceeding in London, and is the 'Charlie' who 'sends you his best love' in Douglas's letter to Wilde of 15 May 1895, one of only three Douglas-to-Wilde letters recovered. Nearly four years later, in exile at Napoule, Wilde had a presentation copy of The Importance of Being Earnest addressed to him and asked Reggie Turner after him.
bio_note: All facts from Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000) with printed folios confirmed. The Douglas Autobiography (1929) description and the 15 May 1895 letter it glosses are p. 649 n. 3 (repo PDF 700); the note prints the Douglas letter in full and appends the Autobiography sentence. The presentation copy and Wilde's enquiry after him are p. 1122 (PDF 1168), in Wilde to Reginald Turner, [postmark 3 February 1899]. NOT read so far (pointers): the remaining General Index locators 811, 830, 837, 878, 1132. DATES: NONE RECORDED. Searched so far: the whole OCR mirror of the Complete Letters (2000) for every occurrence of the name, plus the edition's General Index; Frankel, Oscar Wilde: The Unrepentant Years (2017), repo PDF, the fullest scholarly account of the exile years; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008) and Murray, Bosie (2020), repo PDFs. The only quantity in the record is relative and remains an inference that is deliberately not entered: Douglas's Autobiography (1929), as printed in the editors' note at p. 649 n. 3, calls him 'a charming boy about a couple of years younger than myself'. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted, and no surname search is possible beyond 'a son of Colonel Hickey', which would need an Army List to pursue.
